Method: watch one door on screen while polling the save, and read which enumerator changes - the same wall-clock join that bound the class ids. WHICH frame it encodes - placement, spawn, or position at first save - and the physical unit of either quantity are unmeasured. DoorData and TreasureBoxMap carry no Transform, so the confirmation available is monsters-only. Watching one actor across two runs to see whether its key is stable would separate the readings

PlayzoneData is a shrinking-circle mechanic (DmgCircle and SafeCircle, each a Vector2D centre plus a radius, plus FinialSafeCircleLocation and ElapseTime). In this capture the damage and safe circles are identical to the bit, so the zone had not started moving. Whether they ever diverge, and whether the talent Gyldenmist Tolerance names this mechanic, are both UNMEASURED - do not write the talent binding down until something observed connects them

Verified against the real bytes, not a synthetic. The original error: the value was characterised with a permissive pattern that pure digits also match, then redact() was tested against a fabricated ALPHABETIC input whose shape occurs nowhere in the data. A guard tested on an invented input proves nothing about the data. The residual - an alphabetic value under a device key would not be caught - is a real but UNOBSERVED shape and is already recorded as a stated limit in the redact module docstring. Widening for it was considered and declined: the module's discipline is that rules are added on measurement, and the DEVICE_ID rule itself is documented as a renaming rather than a widening.
